proposed_fixes.title: Investigate Chrome zoning eligibility and snap-hotkey routing
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Chrome's foreground window is rejected or no active zone layout is found in one reported path; the elevation and hotkey symptoms may have different causes.
plan: Reproduce the initial elevated-versus-unelevated Chrome behavior and the later Win+Arrow behavior independently.
Check FancyZones override settings, foreground eligibility, and active layout before changing routing.
Fix the verified path and add coverage without regressing Shift-drag or Windows snap fallback.

reproduce.title: Investigate Chrome zoning eligibility and snap-hotkey routing
prerequisites: Windows with Chrome and an active FancyZones layout
setup: Enable Win+Arrow override and Shift-drag zoning in Settings.
steps: Compare zoning normal and elevated Chrome as described in the original report.
Separately test Win+Arrow and Shift-drag on normal Chrome.
Check the same shortcuts on another ordinary window.
